title: Why Adding More People Makes Late Projects Later
alt_title_1: Brooks's Law Explained: The N(N-1)/2 Coordination Trap
alt_title_2: Why Tiny 3-Person Pods Out-Ship Crowded 12-Person Committees
description_hook: In his classic 1975 book 'The Mythical Man-Month', IBM engineering manager Fred Brooks explained why adding people to a late project delays it further: communication channels explode by N*(N-1)/2. Here is why cutting scope beats adding headcount.

scenes.headline: Why Extra Help Pushes Deadlines Further Away
bullets: Project slips behind -> managers add 3 extra people
Delivery slows down instead of speeding up
scenes.narration: When a critical software or creative project falls behind schedule, adding three helpful teammates almost always pushes the finish line even further away.

scenes.headline: Communication Channels Explode by N(N-1)/2
bullets: 3 builders = only 3 communication links to align
scenes.narration: In his 1975 classic The Mythical Man-Month, IBM engineering manager Fred Brooks showed why: communication channels scale by N times N minus one over two. Three builders have three links; ten create forty-five.

scenes.headline: Onboarding Steals Hours From Your Top Builders
scenes.left_body: Adds 5 newcomers late -> top builders stuck onboarding & syncing
scenes.right_body: 2-3 aligned builders + trimmed scope -> ships cleanly on time
scenes.narration: Every newcomer requires onboarding from your busiest builders right when time is scarcest, turning productive creation hours into status calls, handoffs, and merge conflicts.

scenes.headline: Cut Non-Essential Scope, Never Add Chaos
scenes.stat_label: LEAN PODS + TIGHT SCOPE = FAST ITERATION
scenes.stat_subtext: Fewer handoffs compound shipping velocity week after week
scenes.narration: When a deadline slips, resist throwing headcount at the problem. Cut non-essential scope, shield a tiny two-to-three-person pod from meetings, and ship the core asset first.

scenes.headline: Small Aligned Pods Beat Crowded Committees
scenes.stat_label: FIRST LEVER WHEN TIMELINES GET TIGHT
bullets: Simplify Version 1.0 down to what truly matters
Protect small ownership pods from calendar bloat
scenes.narration: Shrink scope before expanding headcount, because tiny aligned pods out-ship crowded committees every single quarter.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin execution rule based on Fred Brooks (1975)
